sights.n: Nirai Kanai Bridge overlook (ニライカナイ橋)
sights.w: A sweeping U-shaped road bridge that switchbacks down the Chinen hillside with the Pacific and Kudaka Island ahead — best seen from the tunnel-top viewpoint. It appears in the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', which earned Nanjō a place among the Anime Tourism Association's 88 anime pilgrimage sites.
sights.anime: The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — bridge shown in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site

sights.n: Kouri Ōhashi Bridge & Kouri Island (古宇利大橋・古宇利島)
sights.w: The 1,960 m toll-free bridge (2005) from Yagaji Island across emerald shallows to Kouri, the 'Island of Love' — one of Okinawa's signature drives, with beaches, Heart Rock and garlic-shrimp trucks at the far end.

sights.n: Ama Beach, Zamami Island (阿真ビーチ)
sights.w: The quieter of Zamami's two main beaches, on the southwest shore facing the uninhabited islets of Gahi and Agenashiku; sea turtles graze offshore.

sights.n: Takatsukiyama Observatory, Zamami (高月山展望台)
sights.w: Hilltop lookout over Zamami village, Furuzamami Beach and the scattered Kerama islands — the classic Kerama Blue panorama.

sights.n: Pokémon Center Okinawa, Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom (ポケモンセンターオキナワ)
sights.address: Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom 1F, 1 Raikamu, Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa 901-2306, Japan
sights.w: Okinawa's first Pokémon Center (opened 11 Aug 2022, Japan's 16th), themed on the island's nature: Pikachu and Arcanine greet you at the entrance, with Okinawa-only goods and a video zone. Pair it with a hunt for the prefecture's 16 Pokémon manhole 'Poké Lids'.
sights.anime: Pokémon — the prefecture's only Pokémon Center, with Okinawa-exclusive merchandise

sights.w: One of the Eight Shrines of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, perched on a forested limestone ridge in Sueyoshi Park; a stone path climbs through jungle to the rebuilt hall — a quiet counterpoint to Shuri Castle.

The surviving stone gate of the Ryūkyū royal temple founded in 1527, where all who entered — even the king — had to dismount; the temple was destroyed in WWII but the gate was restored and has been an Important Cultural Property since 1972, fronting a small park.
sights.k: Ryukyu royal temple gate (Important Cultural Property)

sights.address: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: The 'Dragon Depths' pond below Shuri Castle, dug in 1427 under King Shō Hashi by the official Kaiki to entertain Chinese envoys; the classic reflection view of the castle walls.

sights.n: Okinawa Karate Kaikan (沖縄空手会館)
sights.w: The prefecture's home of karate, opened March 2017 on a 3.8 ha site near Naha Airport: a museum on the art's Okinawan origins, training dojo and the ceremonial Shureikan hall.

sights.n: Michi-no-Eki Kadena observation deck (道の駅かでな)
sights.w: Roadside station beside Kadena Air Base whose rooftop observation deck looks straight across the runway — the place locals and plane-spotters watch fighter jets take off and land; Mapple ranks it Okinawa's No. 3 michi-no-eki.

sights.n: Ishigaki-jima Limestone Cave (石垣島鍾乳洞)
sights.w: Japan's southernmost show cave: 3.2 km of limestone formed over some 200,000 years in southern Ishigaki, with a lit walkway through the formations.
